gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on the Synology DS425+ an M.2 storage pool (the SSD that ChatGPT suggested for Audiobookshelf's app data, which Audiobookshelf's docs require to sit on local storage) only works with Synology-verified SSDs. The DS225+ that ChatGPT recommended has no M.2 slots at all, while the UGREEN DXP2800 has two.
standout_why: I compared against racksandwatts.com/guides/best-nas-for-a-homelab-2026 (cited; updated 2026-10-25), which lists CPU, RAM and bays for the DXP2800, DS225+, DXP4800 Plus and DS925+. It states no prices, no total cost with drives and no power draw, and it doesn't mention Audiobookshelf or Calibre-Web. It does say the DS225+ has 'no NVMe', but it doesn't mention Synology's verified-SSD rule for M.2 pools. The DS425+ data sheet was in ChatGPT's results (uncited) and may carry the same footnote, so this is only partly new. My main deliverable for this angle, a priced table of the whole category for today, mostly failed: only the QNAP price could be opened and read.
decides: It supports the DXP2800 as the pick. ChatGPT's own setup advice (app data on an NVMe SSD, 8 GB RAM) works on the DXP2800 with any SSD. On the DS225+ it can't be done (no M.2, 2 GB installed, 6 GB maximum in one slot). On the DS425+ it needs a Synology-verified SSD. The QNAP TS-264-8G ($489 at QNAP's US store) costs more than every DXP2800 price ChatGPT showed and has a 2–4 week lead time.
